finding.claim: The /fetch2 endpoint fetches an attacker-supplied URL with only a scheme check. Attackers can reach internal services, loopback, and cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/). Redirects are followed, and part of the response body is returned.
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5) at views.py:22 (redirects followed by default)

trace.note: url taken from the query string
only checks that the scheme is http or https
requests.get(url) is called with the first 200 bytes of the body returned

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url checks the scheme only. There is no host or IP check, no allowlist, and redirects are not disabled.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; the stronger is_safe_url is used only on /fetch)
verdict.reason: views.py:19 takes url from request.args, views.py:20 only calls the scheme-only is_http_url (validators.py:7), and views.py:22 calls requests.get(url) with redirects followed by default and returns the first 200 bytes of the body, so there is no host or IP guard.

finding.claim: The /fetch endpoint has an IP blocklist, but it is vulnerable to DNS rebinding (TOCTOU). is_safe_url resolves the hostname once to validate it, and requests.get resolves it again to connect. An attacker-controlled DNS server can return a public IP for the check and then an internal IP (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254) for the fetch. This is a lower-confidence candidate that depends on the attacker controlling DNS. Redirects are disabled, which closes the redirect bypass.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
first DNS resolution via socket.getaddrinfo, and every returned address is checked
rejects private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses
requests.get re-resolves the hostname independently, so the validated IP is not pinned

finding.guards_checked: The scheme must be http or https and a hostname must be present. Every resolved address is checked against the private, loopback, link-local and reserved ranges. Redirects are disabled. The resolved IP is not pinned for the request, so a rebinding DNS server with a very low TTL or alternating answers can bypass the check.

verdict.guard_found: is_safe_url: scheme http/https + hostname present (validators.py:12), resolved IPs checked against private/loopback/link-local/reserved (validators.py:14-17), allow_redirects=False (views.py:14). None pins the IP or uses a hostname allowlist, so none closes the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `url` (views.py:11) is validated by a separate getaddrinfo call (validators.py:14) and then re-resolved by requests.get (views.py:14) without pinning the IP, so a rebinding DNS server can pass the check and then be fetched at an internal address.
